findings.problem: The normal is taken from the `cpContactPointSet::normal` field instead of calling `cpArbiterGetNormal(arb)`, which is the API the requirement explicitly names (and what upstream cocos2d-x calls). Behaviourally identical, so this is fidelity/readability only — not a defect.
findings.evidence: Requirement physics_contact: "generateContactData() must read the contact points AND normal from the cpArbiter (cpArbiterGetContactPointSet / cpArbiterGetNormal)". In Chipmunk 7.0.x the two values are the same by construction: cpArbiterGetContactPointSet() sets `set.normal = (arb->swapped ? cpvneg(arb->n) : arb->n)` and cpArbiterGetNormal() returns `cpvmult(arb->n, arb->swapped ? -1 : 1)` — the identical swap-corrected vector. So no sign flip or wrong-orientation bug exists here; only the named-API expectation is unmet.
findings.fix: Change `PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(contactSet.normal)` to `PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(cpArbiterGetNormal(arb))` so the line literally uses the API the requirement names (and matches upstream). No other change needed; `arb` is already in scope.

findings.problem: The failed-dynamic_cast branch returns silently; upstream asserts before returning, so a mis-dispatched event type is invisible in debug builds. This is inherited verbatim from the hollowed base (the diff did not touch it), not introduced by this round.
findings.evidence: Upstream cocos2d-x v4 CCPhysicsContact.cpp begins onEvent with `PhysicsContact* contact = dynamic_cast<PhysicsContact*>(event); if (contact == nullptr) { CCASSERT(false, "PhysicsContact is nullptr"); return; }`. The event name PHYSICSCONTACT_EVENT_NAME is only ever dispatched with a PhysicsContact (CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:350/369/384/396 dispatch `&contact`), so a null cast is a programming error worth asserting on.
findings.fix: Add `CCASSERT(false, "PhysicsContact is nullptr");` before the `return;` inside the `if (contact == nullptr)` block. Release behaviour is unchanged (CCASSERT compiles out).

result.summary: CCPhysicsContact.cpp is behaviourally correct and complete: generateContactData() now reads real arbiter data (null-guard on _contactInfo, rotate _contactData into _preContactData, cpArbiterGetContactPointSet, points[i].pointA per point, count clamped to POINT_MAX which is safe since CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER is 2, normal zeroed when count==0), onEvent() is a byte-for-byte match of upstream's switch — BEGIN/PRESOLVE guard on callback-non-null AND hitTest, call generateContactData() and setResult(ret) (with ret defaulting to true when not hit-tested), while POSTSOLVE/SEPARATE only invoke their void callbacks and never touch _result, exactly matching PhysicsWorld::collisionPreSolveCallback/resetResult() semantics in CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:350-397; and WithGroup::hitTest() now ORs the two shapes' groups (PhysicsShape::getGroup() is public and mirrors PhysicsBody::getGroup(), CCPhysicsShape.h:337 / CCPhysicsBody.cpp:830). I re-verified every cp* call against Chipmunk 7.0.x for arity/argument order/return type (cpArbiterGet/Set Restitution, Friction, SurfaceVelocity, cpArbiterIgnore, cpArbiterGetContactPointSet) — all correct, no swapped arguments, no leaked or double-freed cp objects, and the _contactData/_preContactData rotation plus the destructor's two CC_SAFE_DELETEs leak nothing across repeated BEGIN/PRESOLVE calls. I also re-read the untouched surroundings for planted bugs (WithBodies/WithShapes hitTest symmetric pair checks, checkAvailable's all-null test, the four clone() overloads, _group(CP_NO_GROUP), PHYSICSCONTACT_EVENT_NAME matching CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:46) and found none. Guard tests: no marker words, no hollow/empty/literal-only bodies in this file (the only test_no_hollow_method_bodies and test_no_stub_markers failures come from CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp and CCPhysicsSpatialIndex.cpp, which are still hollow), headers untouched, and this file is not one of the non-friend extension modules. The two findings above are optional upstream-fidelity nits with no effect on physics results; /tmp/cpsyntax/check.sh did not exist on any of three polls, so no compile check was run.

findings.problem: The contactTestBitmask gate uses OR semantics (`(categoryA & testB) | (categoryB & testA)) != 0`), so a pair is reported when only ONE side opts in. cocos2d-x requires BOTH directions to be non-zero before a contact is reported.
findings.evidence: Upstream reference in this very repo, /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:331-334: `if ((shapeA->getCategoryBitmask() & shapeB->getContactTestBitmask()) == 0 || (shapeA->getContactTestBitmask() & shapeB->getCategoryBitmask()) == 0) { contact.setNotificationEnable(false); }` — notification is disabled when EITHER term is zero, i.e. enabled only when both are non-zero. The requirement says filterContact/reporting must use the bitmasks "the way cocos2d-x does". Concrete divergence: shapeA.category=1, shapeA.contactTest=0, shapeB.category=2, shapeB.contactTest=1 -> impl fires begin/preSolve/postSolve/separate events, upstream fires none.
findings.fix: Return `(categoryA & testB) != 0 && (categoryB & testA) != 0;` (keep the two AND terms, replace the bitwise `|` combination with a logical `&&` of both non-zero tests).

findings.problem: installHandler unconditionally overwrites the space's single default collision handler (funcs + userData) without saving or chaining to whatever was already installed, and the destructor never restores it. Since init() takes a PhysicsWorld*, the space it resolves is always a space whose default handler was already claimed by PhysicsWorld::init(). Result: as soon as a PhysicsContactManager is init'd, PhysicsWorld's own contact pipeline (PhysicsContact event dispatch to _eventDispatcher, joint collision-disable filtering, contact.resetResult()) is silently dead for the rest of that space's life; and after the manager is destroyed, managerFromData() returns nullptr so begin/preSolve return cpTrue unconditionally and post/separate do nothing — every collision is force-enabled and no events at all are produced.
findings.evidence: Chipmunk 7.0: there is exactly one default handler per space — `cpCollisionHandler *cpSpaceAddDefaultCollisionHandler(cpSpace *space)` returns `&space->defaultHandler`, so a second caller mutates the same struct. /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:501-507 already does `handler->userData = this; handler->beginFunc = ...collisionBeginCallbackFunc; ...` for the same space. The liveManagers() guard only prevents UB after destruction; it cannot restore the funcs the manager clobbered, and Chipmunk invokes handler->beginFunc unconditionally so they cannot simply be nulled.
findings.fix: Capture the previous handler state before overwriting (e.g. a small struct holding the old beginFunc/preSolveFunc/postSolveFunc/separateFunc/userData keyed by cpSpace*), chain to it from each thunk (`cpBool prev = old.beginFunc ? old.beginFunc(arb, space, old.userData) : cpTrue;` and AND it with this manager's verdict), and restore the saved funcs/userData in ~PhysicsContactManager()/on unregister so the world's pipeline survives.

findings.problem: Event dispatch is gated on filterContact() succeeding: when a pair fails the collision/group filter the thunks return early and dispatch nothing. Upstream keeps the two decisions independent — the contactTest bitmask decides whether the event is *reported*, the category/collision bitmask and group decide only the *bool return* — and dispatches the BEGIN event even when the collision itself is rejected.
findings.evidence: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:300-356: notification is decided first (contactTest masks, line 331), then `ret` is computed from group/collisionBitmask (lines 336-348), then `if (contact.isNotificationEnabled()) { ... _eventDispatcher->dispatchEvent(&contact); }` runs regardless of `ret`, and only the return value is `ret ? contact.resetResult() : false`. A pair with contactTest masks set on both sides but non-overlapping collision masks therefore produces a BEGIN event upstream and no event here.
findings.fix: In each thunk, compute `const bool collides = manager->filterContact(...)` but do not early-return on it: dispatch whenever shouldReportContact() is true, and use `collides` only for the cpBool result (`return collides ? cpTrue : cpFalse;`) / to skip nothing in the void post-solve and separate thunks.

findings.problem: filterContact reproduces upstream's group + category/collision bitmask logic but omits upstream's first filtering stage: bodies connected by a PhysicsJoint whose collision is disabled must not collide. Two bodies joined with setCollisionEnable(false) will still collide through this manager.
findings.evidence: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsWorld.cpp:308-328 runs the joint walk (`for (PhysicsJoint* joint : bodyA->getJoints()) ... if (!joint->isCollisionEnabled()) { ... return false; }`) *before* the bitmask checks. Both accessors needed are public and reachable from this non-friend module: CCPhysicsBody.h:292 `const std::vector<PhysicsJoint*>& getJoints() const`, CCPhysicsJoint.h:96 `bool isCollisionEnabled() const`.
findings.fix: Before the group/bitmask block, iterate `bodyA->getJoints()`; for each joint with `!joint->isCollisionEnabled()`, take the other end (`joint->getBodyA() == bodyA ? joint->getBodyB() : joint->getBodyA()`) and `return false` when it equals bodyB.

findings.problem: info.normal is assigned from cpArbiterGetNormal() before the point count is known and is never zeroed for a zero-point manifold, so a separating/cached arbiter (cpArbiterGetCount() == 0, e.g. inside contactSeparateFunc or for a cached arbiter picked up by processContacts) reports a stale non-zero normal. Upstream reports Vec2::ZERO in exactly that case.
findings.evidence: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsContact.cpp:106: `_contactData->normal = _contactData->count > 0 ? PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(contactSet.normal) : Vec2::ZERO;`. Chipmunk 7.0 `cpArbiterGetCount()` returns 0 once the arbiter reaches the cached/separate state while `arb->n` keeps its last value, so the normal survives the manifold. Callers of getContactNormal(index) get a direction for a contact that has no points.
findings.fix: Move the normal assignment below the count clamp and guard it: `info.normal = count > 0 ? PhysicsHelper::cpv2point(cpArbiterGetNormal(arbiter)) : Vec2::ZERO;`. (Optionally also match upstream's point convention, which stores pointA rather than the pointA/pointB midpoint used on line 170.)

result.summary: The file is a complete, compiling-looking implementation: all 24 header declarations are defined, no marker words, no hollow/literal-only bodies, no use of _cpShapes/_cpSpace/->_body/_delayAddBodies/_delayRemoveBodies, and the header is untouched — so agent_tests/test_physics_sources.py passes for it (the two current failures are CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp and CCPhysicsSpatialIndex.cpp). I verified every Chipmunk 7.0.x call for arity, argument order and return type (cpSpaceAddDefaultCollisionHandler, the four cpCollisionHandler func-pointer typedefs, cpSpaceEachBody/cpBodyEachArbiter iterator signatures, cpArbiterGetShapes/GetNormal/GetCount/GetPointA/GetPointB/GetDepth/TotalImpulse/IsFirstContact/IsRemoval, cpShapeGetUserData, cpBodyGetSpace, cpSpaceIsLocked) — all correct, including the index bound that keeps cpArbiterGetDepth's internal cpAssertHard satisfied, the fabs() on the signed separation, and the deliberate decode-after-walk that avoids cpBodyEachArbiter's temporary arb->swapped flip. PhysicsShape::getGroup() is public and non-const but called through a non-const pointer, so const-correctness holds; there are no raw allocations, so the "no leak/double-free" pool requirement is met. Five defects remain: the contactTestBitmask gate uses OR where cocos2d-x requires both directions (line 198), installHandler clobbers PhysicsWorld's own default collision handler and never restores it (line 382), event dispatch is wrongly gated on the collision filter (line 262 and the three sibling thunks), the joint collision-disable filter stage is missing (line 514), and the contact normal is not zeroed for a zero-point manifold (line 151). Two lesser notes not raised as findings: init() silently skips handler installation when no body of the world is in a space yet (so the first step's begin events can be missed until processContacts runs), and processContacts's late install is skipped while the space is locked.

findings.problem: getContactCount() returns cpArbiterGetCount(_arbiter) raw, with no clamp to the CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER / POINT_MAX bound, and getContactPoints() then uses that unclamped value as the write count into the caller's `outPoints` buffer (lines 148-152). The header signature `void getContactPoints(CollisionPoint* outPoints, int* outCount) const` has no capacity argument, so the only contract the caller can size to is the arbiter contact bound; an unclamped loop is an unbounded write into a fixed-size caller array.
findings.evidence: The requirement focus states the accessors must be "bounds-checked against CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER" — that bound is not applied anywhere in this file. The sibling module completed to standard does exactly this clamp: /workspace/cocos2d-x/cocos/physics/CCPhysicsContactManager.cpp:24-26 declares `const int kMaxContactPoints = 4;` with the comment "Chipmunk never reports more than CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER (2) points per arbiter, so this is a hard bound", and lines 153-162 clamp `count` to [0, kMaxContactPoints] before indexing. cocos2d-x itself fixes the same bound as `PhysicsContactData::POINT_MAX = 4` (CCPhysicsContact.h:46). Note CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER is not exposed by the public "chipmunk/chipmunk.h", which is why the sibling uses a named local constant.
findings.fix: Add an anonymous-namespace constant mirroring the sibling (e.g. `const int kMaxContactPoints = 4; // CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER is 2; PhysicsContactData::POINT_MAX is the engine-side bound`) and clamp in getContactCount(): `int count = cpArbiterGetCount(_arbiter); if (count < 0) count = 0; if (count > kMaxContactPoints) count = kMaxContactPoints; return count;`. getContactPoint/getContactPoints/computeOverlap/computeContactCenter then inherit the bound for free.

findings.problem: `count` is only computed inside `if (outPoints != nullptr)`, so a caller that passes `outPoints == nullptr` to probe how many contacts exist before allocating gets `*outCount == 0` — the pair silently reports "no contacts" for a live, penetrating arbiter. The count query and the fill are conflated.
findings.evidence: The header declares two independent out-parameters (`CollisionPoint* outPoints, int* outCount`) with no capacity argument; the only way a caller can discover the required buffer size through this API is a null-buffer probe, and the requirement lists getContactPoints as a first-class accessor of the contact manifold. Reporting 0 for a valid arbiter contradicts getContactCount() returning non-zero for the same pair.
findings.fix: Hoist the count out of the branch: `int count = getContactCount(); if (outPoints != nullptr) { for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) outPoints[i] = getContactPoint(i); } if (outCount != nullptr) *outCount = count;`

findings.problem: `invalidate()` (lines 70-74) clears only `_arbiter` and `_valid`; it leaves `_ignored` set and leaves `_shapeA`/`_shapeB` pointing at shapes that may already be destroyed. `isIgnored()` is the one accessor with no validity guard at all, so an invalidated pair keeps reporting `isIgnored() == true` from a previous, unrelated arbiter until someone calls init() again.
findings.evidence: Requirement focus: "Every accessor must guard an invalidated pair / null arbiter." Every other accessor in the file opens with `if (_arbiter == nullptr || !_valid)`; isIgnored() does not, and invalidate() does not reset the state it reads. The stale `_shapeA`/`_shapeB` are also the pointers getShapeA()/getShapeB() would hand back the moment `_valid` is set again by any future code path.
findings.fix: Reset the full state in invalidate(): `_arbiter = nullptr; _shapeA = nullptr; _shapeB = nullptr; _valid = false; _ignored = false;` (and/or guard isIgnored() with `return _valid && _ignored;`).

findings.problem: `point.depth` stores the raw signed Chipmunk separation, which is negative while the shapes overlap, whereas computeOverlap() at line 346 takes std::fabs of the same quantity. So for one and the same contact `getContactPoint(i).depth` is negative while `computeOverlap()` is positive — two contradictory meanings for "depth" inside one class.
findings.evidence: cpArbiterGetDepth() returns cpvdot(pointB - pointA, normal), i.e. a signed separation that is negative under penetration — the sibling module documents this verbatim at CCPhysicsContactManager.cpp:171 ("cpArbiterGetDepth() is a signed separation: negative while the shapes overlap") and then normalises it with std::fabs before storing it in `info.depths[i]`. CollisionPoint::depth (CCPhysicsCollisionPair.h:25) is the analogous engine-facing field and should follow the same convention.
findings.fix: Match the house convention: `point.depth = std::fabs(PhysicsHelper::cpfloat2float(cpArbiterGetDepth(_arbiter, index)));` (or, if signed separation is deliberate, drop the fabs in computeOverlap and use `-depth` clamped at 0 so both agree).

result.summary: The file is fully implemented — no hollow bodies, no placeholder markers, all 30 header declarations defined, header untouched, no trailing whitespace/tabs, and `python3 -m pytest agent_tests/test_physics_sources.py` reports zero CollisionPair offenders (the two failures come from CCPhysicsShapeQuery.cpp and CCPhysicsSpatialIndex.cpp, still hollow and owned by other tasks). I verified every cp* call against Chipmunk 7.0.x for arity, argument order and return type: cpArbiterGetShapes(arb,&a,&b), cpArbiterGetNormal(arb) (single-arg 7.0 form, not the 6.x indexed one), cpArbiterGetPointA/PointB/GetDepth(arb,i), cpArbiterTotalImpulse/TotalKE, Get/Set Restitution/Friction/SurfaceVelocity, cpArbiterIsFirstContact/IsRemoval/Ignore, cpShapeGetSensor/GetBody/GetUserData, cpBodyGetVelocityAtWorldPoint(body,point) — all correct. The impulse projections are genuinely right: cpArbiterTotalImpulse sums cpvrotate(n,(jnAcc,jtAcc)) so dot(n) recovers jn and dot(perp(n)) recovers jt exactly, and because Chipmunk negates the whole sum when the arbiter is swapped, the std::fabs on both is the correct choice rather than a lost sign. getContactNormal/getShapes/computeRelativeVelocity are also consistently swap-safe, so computeSeparatingVelocity's sign (positive = separating, normal points A to B) is right. The real gaps are the missing CP_MAX_CONTACTS_PER_ARBITER bound the requirement names explicitly (an unbounded write into a caller buffer that has no capacity argument), the null-buffer count probe in getContactPoints returning 0, an unguarded isIgnored() paired with an incomplete invalidate(), and a self-contradictory sign convention for contact depth. /tmp/cpsyntax/check.sh never appeared (polled three times), so no compile check was possible.
